minutes.headline: Parks Commission tabled a hunting and weapons ban to a third meeting and named Anna Lockwood open space rep
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission met remotely. It discussed a policy for non-departmental beach use, a ban on hunting and weapon discharge on park land, the Marshall Park track, volunteer cleanup days, and the Marshall Park master plan. It also discussed building one policy document and the park revolving fund. Minutes were approved and an open space representative was appointed.

public_comment.topic: Beach capacity limits simultaneous events, and lifeguards would likely cover Sunday morning events.

votes.motion: Approve the November 9th and December 1st minutes.
Appoint Anna Lockwood as the Parks Commission rep to the open space committee.

budget_items.what_was_said: Other towns charge hourly rental fees and require day passes for groups. The commission wants a flat fee covering lifeguard pay and general costs.
Members suggested buying picnic tables from the revolving fund or a line item instead of the master plan.
Possible warrant article for consulting or survey funds, since capital planning ranked the project below the likely funding line. To be discussed in February.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission tabled a hunting, trapping and weapons policy to a third meeting so the public can comment after the draft goes to town counsel.
The commission appointed Anna Lockwood as its representative to the open space committee; the minutes record the vote as not audible.
The recreation director was asked to draft a separate beach group-use policy, with pricing, for the next meeting.
Members discussed a possible warrant article for Marshall Park consulting or survey funds, since capital planning ranked the project below the likely funding line.
The February meeting was set for Friday the 12th at 6:30.

why_it_matters: A ban on hunting and weapon discharge on park land would change what residents may do on public parks, and the tabling leaves a public comment window before any rule is adopted.
A flat beach group-use fee meant to cover lifeguard pay and general costs would set what groups pay to use the beach, and a Marshall Park warrant article would be a funding vote at Town Meeting.
watch_next: February meeting, Friday the 12th at 6:30: beach group-use policy with pricing, the hunting and weapons policy, and Marshall Park funding.
Town counsel's review of the draft hunting, trapping and weapons policy, ahead of public comment.
